title: Fix release @ autocomplete FFF module resolution
description: Release Nexus fails on non-empty @ file autocomplete queries like @/ or @sd with 'Cannot find module @ff-labs/fff-node' from //root/nexus. Investigate the Bun compiled binary/runtime package lookup path for the bundled FFF extension and implement a release-safe fix with regression coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Non-empty @ autocomplete works in source and release-safe execution paths
notes: Validated manually after just release by launching /opt/homebrew/bin/nexus in a PTY, typing @/, and confirming output no longer contains 'Cannot find module'. Found secondary Bun release issue where ffi-rs could not resolve @yuuang/ffi-rs-darwin-arm64; fixed by staging ffi-rs.darwin-arm64.node directly into the ffi-rs package root for release bundles.

title: Implement Nexus parity for built-in Pi selector slash menus
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

The custom Nexus slash UI still falls through to Pi for several built-in slash commands that open selector-style interactive menus. We need explicit parity tasks for each built-in slash command that launches a selector or submenu flow in Pi interactive mode, so Nexus can keep the full interaction inside the custom UI.

Source: node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent/dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js

Included selector-style commands:
- /settings -> showSettingsSelector()
- /scoped-models -> showModelsSelector()
- /model -> handleModelCommand() / showModelSelector()
- /fork -> showUserMessageSelector()
- /tree -> showTreeSelector() with branch-summary follow-up selector
- /resume -> showSessionSelector()
- /login -> showOAuthSelector("login")
- /logout -> showOAuthSelector("logout")

Goal:
- keep these flows inside the custom Nexus slash UI
- stop handing them off to Pi builtin selectors
- add parity coverage for each flow
acceptance_criteria: Every built-in Pi slash command that opens a selector-style interactive menu is tracked as a child issue and implemented inside the Nexus custom slash UI without falling through to Pi builtin selectors

title: Add regression coverage for the Pi-runtime-backed Nexus settings menu
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

We need tests that prove Nexus stays aligned to the installed Pi runtime settings contract.

Work:
- add tests for visible settings item names and ordering
- add tests for submenu options like theme and thinking
- add tests proving removed pseudo-editable items like defaultModel are absent
- add tests for applied actions where deterministic
acceptance_criteria: Tests lock visible runtime-backed settings items, submenu options, and removal of non-Pi pseudo-settings

title: Map Nexus settings actions to Pi-equivalent runtime behavior only
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

Visible settings items must perform the same action Pi performs for that setting. Theme, thinking, transport, toggles, and numeric options must use Pi-equivalent behavior. Items not in Pi /settings must not be handled here.

Work:
- implement write/apply behavior per Pi runtime settings callbacks
- ensure theme, thinking, image, transport, and UI settings behave like Pi
- route model/provider handling out of the settings menu
acceptance_criteria: Every visible Nexus settings item applies the same behavior category Pi uses; non-settings flows like model/provider are not handled in the settings submenu

title: Read Pi runtime settings-selector config for visible settings items and options
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

Nexus must derive the settings menu from Pi runtime source instead of duplicating a hand-maintained list.

Work:
- inspect Pi runtime settings-selector inputs from the installed package
- build a runtime reader that exposes the exact visible settings items and allowed values/options
- preserve Pi ordering and submenu shape
acceptance_criteria: Nexus reads the live Pi settings-selector contract at runtime and exposes the same visible items, ordering, and option values

title: Remove generic merged-settings editing from the Nexus slash menu
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

The current settings branch builds leaves from Object.entries of merged settings and treats non-boolean values as pseudo-editable items. That behavior is incorrect and must be removed.

Work:
- delete the generic merged-settings leaf generation path
- remove non-Pi settings entries from the custom settings UI
- keep only runtime-derived settings items that Pi /settings actually exposes
acceptance_criteria: The settings menu no longer uses raw merged settings as the editable source; items like defaultModel/defaultProvider no longer appear as editable settings entries

title: Rewrite Nexus settings menu to use Pi runtime settings selector contract only
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

The current Nexus slash settings menu incorrectly treats merged JSON settings as a generic editable schema. That diverges from Pi. We need to remove that behavior and rebuild the Nexus settings menu so it derives items, values, and submenu options from Pi runtime settings-selector behavior only, with no fallback path and no compatibility layer.

Scope:
- remove the raw merged-settings-as-editor approach
- read the live Pi settings selector contract at runtime
- show only the settings Pi /settings actually exposes
- use the exact Pi-backed values and option lists for those items
- route non-settings behavior like model/provider selection out of this menu
- add regression tests for the Pi-runtime-backed settings menu contract

Non-goals:
- do not keep the old generic settings editor path
- do not add compatibility fallbacks for older Pi contracts
- do not keep settings entries that Pi does not expose in /settings
acceptance_criteria: Nexus settings menu is derived only from Pi runtime settings-selector behavior; non-Pi settings entries are removed; submenu options match Pi runtime values; tests lock the runtime-backed contract

title: Restore full default Pi slash-command parity in the Nexus slash menu
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

The custom Nexus slash menu currently does not guarantee parity with the default built-in Pi command set. That is a regression. The replacement slash UI must enumerate and surface the same default Pi commands that users would expect upstream, in addition to bundled extension commands, prompt templates, and skill commands where applicable.

Start by treating the upstream Pi README command table as the source-backed baseline for default commands, then verify the actual runtime command discovery path against that baseline. For each default command below, add an explicit verification item and wire it into the Nexus slash menu if missing.

Default Pi command baseline from `node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent/README.md`:
- [ ] `/login`
- [ ] `/logout`
- [ ] `/model`
- [ ] `/scoped-models`
- [ ] `/settings`
- [ ] `/resume`
- [ ] `/new`
- [ ] `/name`
- [ ] `/session`
- [ ] `/tree`
- [ ] `/fork`
- [ ] `/compact`
- [ ] `/copy`
- [ ] `/export`
- [ ] `/share`
- [ ] `/reload`
- [ ] `/hotkeys`
- [ ] `/changelog`
- [ ] `/quit`

Required implementation steps:
1. confirm the complete upstream default-command source of truth from Pi docs and runtime APIs
2. compare that list against what the custom Nexus slash menu currently exposes
3. update command discovery so built-in Pi commands are included, not only extension-registered commands captured by the local registry proxy
4. keep bundled extension commands, prompt templates, and skill commands working after the change
5. add focused tests proving the custom slash menu contains the full default Pi command baseline

Testing instructions:
- add deterministic tests for slash-menu item generation
- assert every baseline command above is present by name in the produced menu model
- add at least one regression test specifically for `/fork`
- if runtime command ordering is defined by Pi, preserve it or document intentional grouping differences
- do not hardcode fake command samples; use the real command-discovery path or a source-backed fixture that mirrors Pi defaults exactly
acceptance_criteria: The custom Nexus slash menu includes the full default Pi command baseline, including /fork; tests assert presence of each default command; built-in Pi commands, extension commands, prompt templates, and skill commands all remain available in the custom slash UI

title: Port @ provider and slash provider onto the generic trigger controller
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

After the generic trigger controller exists, the @ file finder and slash menu must both run through the same controller contract. Their differences should be limited to provider logic: query parsing, item loading, preview rendering, and completion/apply behavior.

Implementation notes:
- adapt FFF-backed @ provider to the generic controller
- adapt dynamic slash command/settings provider to the generic controller
- remove remaining direct editor branches that special-case slash vs at modal behavior
- keep folder-aware @ completion working
acceptance_criteria: @ and / use the same controller entrypoints and input-routing path; provider differences are limited to content loading, preview, and apply behavior; folder picks still apply correctly in @
notes:
Progress:
- command parity fixed separately via built-in Pi slash command discovery for the custom slash menu
- PromptlineEditor now uses shared active-session lookup and shared routeTriggerInput logic

Remaining:
- @ and / still use separate refresh/create branches rather than one provider contract
- provider port is partial, not complete

title: Add deterministic e2e coverage for unified Neo trigger behavior
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

We need regression coverage that proves @ and / behave identically at the controller level and do not regress on paste/cancel/reopen cases.

E2E test instructions:
- use the virtual-terminal harness, not mocks, for all trigger interaction tests
- add one test that types @, filters results, cancels with Esc, then confirms further typing does not reopen until a new typed @ starts a fresh session
- add one test that types /, filters results, cancels with Ctrl+C, then confirms further typing does not reopen until a new typed / starts a fresh session
- add one test that pastes text beginning with /path or OCR-like absolute paths and confirms slash UI does not auto-open
- add one test that verifies both @ and / ignore stale trigger sessions after programmatic text replacement or submit handling
- add one parity-focused test that asserts the same lifecycle events occur for @ and / through the shared controller hooks
- keep tests deterministic and self-contained; avoid timing races by waiting on virtual-terminal renders/events explicitly
acceptance_criteria: Virtual-terminal e2e tests cover typed-start, filter, cancel, paste, reopen, invalidation, and parity for @ and /; tests fail before the fix and pass after it
notes:
Progress:
- added deterministic regression tests for built-in slash parity, slash menu rendering, and trigger-session invalidation/routing

Remaining:
- the dedicated virtual-terminal e2e matrix requested in the issue is not complete yet, especially typed-start/cancel/reopen flows inside the real Neo editor loop

title: Build generic Neo trigger-session controller
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

Neo still contains trigger-specific branches for @ and / during activation, invalidation, and input routing. We need one controller that owns trigger start, active-session tracking, cancellation, invalidation after edits, and overlay open/close behavior.

Implementation notes:
- model trigger sessions explicitly from typed-start intent only
- clear sessions on Ctrl+C, Esc, submit, paste, and programmatic text replacement
- expose a provider interface so @ and / plug in content without changing controller behavior
- remove remaining behavior differences between slash and at sessions
acceptance_criteria: One controller module owns trigger lifecycle for both @ and /; trigger session starts only from typed trigger key; cancel/invalidation behavior is identical for both triggers; provider API isolates content-specific logic
notes:
Progress:
- introduced shared trigger session helpers and generic input-routing helper modules
- PromptlineEditor now routes active trigger sessions through shared session state and shared modal lookup instead of separate slash-first branches
- added regression tests for slash session invalidation and routing behavior

Remaining:
- trigger refresh/create logic is still split between @ and / provider-specific branches inside refreshTriggerModal
- paste/programmatic replacement invalidation still needs deeper end-to-end coverage

title: Unify Neo trigger controller for @ and / overlays
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

The Neo editor currently has partially unified trigger behavior for @ and /, but their live input-routing and modal lifecycle still differ. This causes regressions like slash reopening unexpectedly, paste-path false positives, and inconsistent cancel/reopen behavior between triggers.

This issue tracks the remaining work to create one generic trigger controller in Neo that owns trigger session lifecycle, modal launch, cancellation, invalidation, and input routing for @, /, and future trigger prefixes like #. Trigger-specific code should be limited to modal content/providers only.

Scope:
- build one generic trigger-session controller for Neo
- make @ and / use the exact same behavior path
- preserve FFF-backed @ content and slash-menu content as pluggable providers
- cover typed-start, cancel, paste, reopen, and invalidation cases with deterministic e2e tests

Non-goals:
- do not redesign modal visuals beyond what is needed for behavior parity
- do not expand settings/features unrelated to trigger behavior
- do not add new trigger prefixes yet; only leave the controller ready for them
design: Keep behavior in Neo modules, not content-specific branches. The generic controller should manage typed trigger start, active-session tracking, input routing, close semantics, invalidation on text changes, and overlay reuse. Trigger-specific providers should only supply query parsing, item loading, preview content, and completion application.
acceptance_criteria: One generic trigger controller owns @ and / session lifecycle; @ and / differ only by provider/content; pasted paths or image OCR text must not auto-open slash UI; cancel with Ctrl+C/Esc must fully clear the active trigger session; deterministic virtual-terminal e2e coverage proves parity for @ and / behavior
